Surah At-Takwir (The Folding Up)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. "Kuwwirat" means its light is gone, from "kawwartu al-'imamah" (I wound the turban), when you wrap it, i.e., its light is wrapped up tightly, so its spreading out and its diffusion across the horizons is gone. The "al-shams" (the sun) is in the nominative as the subject (bi-l-fa'iliyyah), and the one who raises it is a hidden verb (fi'l mudmar) which "kuwwirat" explains, because "idha" (when) requires a verb, due to the meaning of condition (shart) that it contains.
﴿And when the stars fall, falling,﴾ — i.e., they drop down.
And when the mountains are set in motion (﴿وَإذا الجِبالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾), away from the face of the earth and removed far away; or they are made to move through the air, like the moving of clouds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 4:

﴿And when the pregnant camels are left neglected﴾, plural of "ʿushara'" (a she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months; the name then continues to apply to her until she gives birth, at the completion of the year),

﴿ʿuṭṭilat﴾, were left unattended (ahmilat). Her owners neglected her (ʿaṭṭalahā ahluhā), being occupied with themselves, and they used to hold her back when she reached this state, because of her value to them, and they would leave idle those that were less than her. "ʿUtilat", with the light form (takhfif), is from al-Bizzi.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 5:

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾: they are brought together from every direction. Qatadah said: "Every creature is gathered, even the flies, for retribution (al-qisas). When judgment has been passed among them, they are turned back into dust, and nothing of them remains except what brings joy to the children of Adam, such as the peacock and the like." And it is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "Their gathering (hashruha) is their death." It is said, when the year (al-sanah, drought) has ravaged the people and their wealth: "The year has gathered them (hasharathum al-sanah)."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 6:

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, "سُجِرَتْ" (sujjirat), "Makki and Basri" (readings), from "sajara al-tannur" (sajara al-tannūr), meaning when he filled it with firewood, i.e., they are filled, and some of them are made to burst into others, until they become one single sea. It is also said: they are filled with fire, to torment the people of the Fire.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: each soul is joined with its like, the righteous with the righteous in Paradise, and the wicked with the wicked in the Fire. Or the spirits are joined to the bodies, or to their records and their deeds. Or the souls of the believers are joined to the wide-eyed houris (al-hur al-‘in), and the souls of the disbelievers to the devils (al-shayatin).

The buried alive (al-Mawudah), the girl who was buried alive. The Arabs used to bury their daughters alive for fear of poverty and fear of their being enslaved.

﴿Is asked﴾: a gentle questioning, so that she would say, "I was killed without any sin," or so that she would point to her killer. Or it is a rebuke to her killer, by turning the address away from him, as in His words: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:116), and the rest of the verse.

Surah 81 (al-Takwir), verse 9:

﴿For what sin was she killed?﴾ And with the doubled letter (tashdid), "yuqatal" (read as yuzayyidu? no: this is a variant reading); and in it is evidence that the children of polytheists are not punished, and that punishment does not occur without sin.

Wait, I need to render this accurately. Here is the faithful translation:

﴿For what sin was she killed?﴾ And [it is read] with the doubled letter (tashdid) as "quttilat" (ruined in the emphatic form, from the doubled verb). In it is evidence that the children of polytheists are not punished, and that punishment does not occur without a sin.

﴿And when the pages are laid open﴾. Futihat (opened), with the lightened reading (takhfif): Madani, Shami, 'Asim, Sahl and Ya'qub. The intended meaning is the pages of deeds: a person's record is folded up at his death, then unfolded (nushira) when he is called to account. It is also permissible that the meaning is: "they are spread out among their owners," i.e., they are distributed among them.
And when the sky is stripped away (﴿وَإذا السَماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾). Al-Zajjaj said: it is pulled off, as a roof is pulled off.

﴿And when the Blazing Fire is kindled﴾: it was kindled with intense kindling. The reading with the doubled letter (sa''irat) is that of al-Shāmī (the Syrian reader), al-Madanī (the Medinan reader), and ʿĀṣim, except Ḥammād and Yaḥyā, and it is for emphasis (intensification). [p. 607]

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 81, verse 13:**

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾, it is brought near to the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), like His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the righteous, not far away﴾ [Qaf: 31]. These are twelve characteristics: six of them in this world, and the remainder in the Hereafter. There is no absolute pause (waqf mutlaq) from the beginning of the surah to "ma ahdarat" (what it has presented), because the governing word of the accusative (*'amil al-nasb*) in "*idha al-shams*" (when the sun) and in what is conjoined to it is the response (*jawab*), which is:

﴿A soul will know﴾, meaning every soul. Because the breath would run out at every verse, pausing (waqf) was permitted at the end of each verse.

﴿what it has brought forward﴾, of good and evil.

﴿So I swear not﴾: "lā" (لا) is superfluous (zāʾida, meaning it adds emphasis without changing the sense).

﴿by the receding ones﴾: i.e., by the returning ones. "Bayna tarā al-najm fī ākhir al-burj idh karra rājiʿan ilā awwalihi": while you see the star at the end of the constellation (burj) when it turns back, returning to its beginning.

**Surah 81, verse 16: "al-Jawari al-Kunnas"**

﴿Al-Jawari﴾: the ones that run (al-sayyara, "the wanderers").

﴿Al-Kunnas﴾: the ones that hide (al-ghuyyab, "the concealed"). It is derived from "kanasa al-wahsh" (the wild beast), meaning when it enters its kinas (lair). It has been said: they are the five planets: Bahram (Mars), Zuhal (Saturn), Utarid (Mercury), al-Zuhra (Venus), and al-Mushtari (Jupiter). They run alongside the sun and the moon, and they retrograde until they are concealed beneath the light of the sun. So their khunus is their retrogression (ruju'uha), and their kunus is their disappearance (ikhtifa'uha) beneath the light of the sun. It has also been said: they are all the stars.

ﷻ "By the night when it turns its back" (Q. 81:17). Al-Nasafi glosses: "when it comes with its darkness, or when it departs; it is from the words with contradictory meanings (al-adhdad)."

Note on the translation: The Arabic ﴿واللَيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ is rendered as the Qur'anic quotation, with the verb 'asa'sa ("turns its back" / "departs") as the primary sense. The gloss that follows is translated as it stands.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an,

﴿is the word of a noble messenger﴾, i.e., Jibril (peace be upon him), and the Qur'an was attributed to him only because he is the one who brought it down,

﴿honored﴾, with his Lord.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 20:

﴿Possessed of power﴾, capability for what he is charged with, not incapable of it, nor weak,

﴿with the Lord of the Throne﴾, with Allah,

﴿esteemed﴾, possessing rank and standing. And since the state of standing is according to the state of the one who holds it, He said: ﴿with the Lord of the Throne﴾, to indicate the greatness of his station and standing.

﴿Muṭā'in thamma﴾ (obeyed there): that is, in the heavens, where those within them obey him; or in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, that is, in the presence of Allah, where His angels brought near obey him, acting upon His command and returning to His judgment.

﴿Amīn﴾ (trustworthy): over the revelation.

﴿Wa ma sahibukum﴾ — "Your companion" — meaning Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿bi-majnun﴾ — "is not a madman," as the disbelievers claim. This is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam).

**Surah 81, verse 23 (Commentary of al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil)**

﴿And he certainly saw him﴾: Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Jibril (peace be upon them both), in his (true) form.

﴿On the clear horizon﴾: at the rising-place of the sun.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 81, verse 24:

﴿And he is not, concerning the Unseen﴾: that is, Muhammad is not (withholding) concerning the revelation.

﴿Stingy﴾: that is, not miserly, from "al-dann" (ضَنّ), which is stinginess. That is: he does not withhold the revelation as the soothsayers (kuhhan) withhold, out of desire for the gift (al-hulwan). Rather, he teaches it as he was taught, and he does not conceal anything of what he was taught.

﴿Suspect﴾: read by Makki, Abu 'Amr and Ali (as "bi-zanin"), that is: accused, so that he would diminish anything of what was revealed to him, or add to it, from "al-zinna" (ظِنَّة), which is accusation.

**Verse 81:25 — "And it is not the word of an accursed devil."**

﴿And it is not﴾, i.e., the Qur'an is not,

﴿the word of an accursed devil﴾, expelled (ṭarīd). This is like His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 210], meaning: it is not the word of one of those who steal hearing (al-mustaraqah lil-sam'), nor the inspiration of them to their allies among the soothsayers (kahanah).

Then where will you go?

This is a question of misguidance directed at them, like the saying addressed to one who leaves the main road and wanders off, going crookedly or taking the side paths: "Where are you going?!" Their situation is depicted by his situation in abandoning the truth and turning away from it to falsehood.

Al-Zajjaj (Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, the grammarian and exegete) said: "Its meaning is: Which path will you take that is clearer than this way that has been made clear to you?!"

Al-Junayd (Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd, the Sufi master) said: "Then where will you go away from Us, when there is not a thing except that it is with Us?!"
Verse 27 of Surah al-Takwir: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ (It is) only an admonition to the creation.

﴿For whoever among you wills﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "al-'alamin" (the worlds).

﴿to go straight﴾: that is, the Qur'an is a reminder for whoever wills uprightness (al-istiqamah). It means that those who will uprightness by entering into Islam are the ones who benefit from the reminder, so it is as though it were not addressed to anyone else, even though all of them are being admonished.

(p-٦٠٩)﴿And you will not will﴾, [meaning] the uprightness (istiqama, steadfastness on the straight path),

﴿unless God wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾, the Owner of all creation.
